en.title: Maximum Sum of Rhombic Area
en.description:
The rhombus region of radius r is the set of cells whose Manhattan distance to the center plus one does not exceed r, that is, |row difference|+|column difference|<r. Considering only centers whose entire rhombus lies inside the matrix, find the maximum of these region sums.

The parts marked 'added by this site' and the standard input/output protocol were explicitly compiled by this site; they do not mean the original problem has other unstated rules.
en.input: The first line contains rows cols radius; then rows lines of the matrix follow. Ranges added by this site: 1≤rows,cols≤200, 1≤radius≤200, |cell|≤10^6. If no complete rhombus exists, output 0.
en.output: Output the maximum region sum; when the radius is so large that no complete region exists, output 0.
en.explanation: See the accompanying editorial for the approach, proof of correctness, and complexity.
